system: You are an analyst who writes clear, concise business reports.
prompt:
Write a report of 5 to 8 sentences for the leadership team at Brightloom on business metrics for April 2026, based on this data.

Company: Brightloom
Period: April 2026

Data:
- Trial-to-paid conversion: 22.4%
- Trial-to-paid conversion in the previous month: 20.3%
- Change in trial-to-paid conversion vs the previous month, in percentage points: 2.1 pp
- Monthly churn: 1.8%
- Monthly churn in the previous month: 1.7%
- Change in monthly churn vs the previous month, in percentage points: 0.1 pp
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC): 46 GBP
- Customer acquisition cost (CAC) in the previous month: 44 GBP
- Change in customer acquisition cost (CAC) vs the previous month: 4.5%
- Net revenue retention (NRR): 103%
- Net revenue retention (NRR) in the previous month: 100%
- Change in net revenue retention (NRR) vs the previous month, in percentage points: 3 pp
- Monthly recurring revenue (MRR): 153,460 GBP
- Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) in the previous month: 150,254 GBP
- Change in monthly recurring revenue (MRR) vs the previous month: 2.1%
- Verdict on the change in net revenue retention (NRR) vs the previous month, in percentage points: strong growth

Notes for the report:
[s1] Customer success note, "Renewal": Avalon Schools renewed its contract for 3 years and added 158 seats.

Use only the information in the data: do not add figures, names, causes or predictions that are not there. Write only the report, in prose, with no headings or lists.
raw: In April 2026 Brightloom’s trial‑to‑paid conversion rose to 22.4%, an improvement of 2.1 percentage points over the prior month’s 20.3%. Monthly churn ticked up slightly to 1.8%, representing a 0.1‑point increase from 1.7% in March. Customer acquisition cost grew to £46, a 4.5 % rise compared with the previous month’s £44 spend per new customer. Net revenue retention reached 103%, up 3 percentage points from 100% and characterized as strong growth. Monthly recurring revenue climbed to £153,460, a 2.1 % increase over the prior month’s £150,254. On the customer‑success side, Avalon Schools renewed its contract for three years and added 158 seats, further supporting the positive revenue trends.
